emmer.name: Emmer wheat
emmer.summary: A hybrid wheat species domesticated in the Near East, one of the first crops grown there; widely farmed in the ancient world, it survives today mainly in mountain regions.

merimde-culture.name: Merimde culture
merimde-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture of the western Nile Delta in Lower Egypt, dated to about 4800-4300 BC, corresponding to the later Faiyum A and Badari cultures.

kerma-culture.name: Kerma culture
kerma-culture.summary: An early civilization and kingdom in ancient Nubia, in what is now Sudan, flourishing from about 2500 to 1500 BCE and rivaling Egypt before Egypt's New Kingdom absorbed it.

faiyum.name: Faiyum
faiyum.summary: A city in Egypt's Faiyum Oasis, about 100 kilometres southwest of Cairo, and one of the country's oldest cities owing to its strategic location.

naqada-culture.name: Naqada culture
naqada-culture.summary: A Chalcolithic Predynastic Egyptian culture (about 4000–3000 BC) named for the town of Naqada, spanning phases Naqada I, II and III with early craft specialization and trade.

tasian-culture.name: Tasian culture
tasian-culture.summary: One of the oldest possible Predynastic cultures of Upper Egypt, dating to around 4500 BC and known for the earliest black-topped pottery, though some scholars doubt it is truly distinct.

a-group-culture.name: A-Group culture
a-group-culture.summary: The first powerful society in ancient Nubia, flourishing between the Nile's First and Second Cataracts from the 4th millennium BC until around 2900 BC.

lower-nubia.name: Lower Nubia
lower-nubia.summary: Northernmost part of ancient Nubia, now largely submerged under Lake Nasser after the Aswan High Dam's construction, with its monuments relocated in a major 20th-century rescue effort.

badarian-culture.name: Badarian culture
badarian-culture.summary: The earliest known farming culture of Upper Egypt, flourishing between about 4400 and 4000 BC and possibly emerging as early as 5000 BC.

institute-for-the-study-of-ancient-cultu.name: Oriental Institute
institute-for-the-study-of-ancient-cultu.summary: A research institute and museum of the University of Chicago, founded in 1919 by Egyptologist James Henry Breasted, that studies ancient Near Eastern and North African civilizations.
institute-for-the-study-of-ancient-cultu.source_title: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures

qustul.name: Qustul
qustul.summary: An archaeological cemetery on the Nile's eastern bank in Lower Nubia, near Ballana, with records from the A-Group culture, Egypt's New Kingdom, and the X-Group culture; now submerged under Lake Nasser.

hoggar-mountains.name: Hoggar Mountains
hoggar-mountains.summary: A highland region of about 550,000 square kilometres in the central Sahara in southern Algeria, home to Algeria's tallest peak, Mount Tahat.

tibesti-mountains.name: Tibesti Mountains
tibesti-mountains.summary: A mountain range in the central Sahara, mostly in northern Chad, home to the Toubou people and site of the highest peaks in Chad and Libya.

cataracts-of-the-nile.name: Second Cataract
cataracts-of-the-nile.summary: One of the shallow, rocky stretches of the Nile between Khartoum and Aswan, broken by boulders, islets and rapids.

djer.name: Djer
djer.summary: Third pharaoh of ancient Egypt's First Dynasty, who reigned for about 40 years around the mid-31st century BC.

djet.name: Djet
djet.summary: Fourth pharaoh of Egypt's First Dynasty, ruling around 2980 BCE as successor to Djer; his Horus name meant 'Serpent of Horus'.

first-dynasty-of-egypt.name: First Dynasty of Egypt
first-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: First series of Egyptian kings to rule a unified Egypt, following the unification of Upper and Lower Egypt, dated to roughly the 32nd to 31st century BC.

serekh.name: Serekh
serekh.summary: A rectangular enclosure in Egyptian hieroglyphs, usually topped by a Horus falcon, used to mark a royal name; it predates the better-known cartouche by centuries.

second-dynasty-of-egypt.name: Second Dynasty of Egypt
second-dynasty-of-egypt.summary: A line of rulers of ancient Egypt from about 2890 to 2686 BC, one of the most obscure periods in Egyptian history, best known for its last ruler, Khasekhemwy.

buhen.name: Buhen
buhen.summary: Ancient Egyptian settlement on the Nile below the Second Cataract in what is now Sudan, founded as an Old Kingdom colonial town known for copper smelting and later fortified as a frontier garrison.

national-museum-of-sudan.name: National Museum of Sudan
national-museum-of-sudan.summary: War-damaged former museum in Khartoum that once held about 100,000 objects spanning Nubian and Kushite history to Sudan's Christian and Islamic periods, established in 1971.

gebel-el-arak-knife.name: Gebel el-Arak Knife
gebel-el-arak-knife.summary: An ivory and flint knife from about 3450-3400 BC showing Mesopotamian influence, bought in Cairo in 1914 and now displayed in the Louvre.

hierakonpolis.name: Hierakonpolis
hierakonpolis.summary: The religious and political capital of Upper Egypt around 3200–3100 BC, centre of worship of the falcon god Horus, and site where the Narmer Palette and an early painted tomb were found.

nabta-playa.name: Nabta Playa
nabta-playa.summary: A prehistoric basin in Egypt's Nubian Desert, site of one of the earliest Nubian Neolithic settlements, dated to around 7500 BC.

wadi-halfa.name: Wadi Halfa
wadi-halfa.summary: A city in northern Sudan near the Egyptian border, surrounded by ancient Nubian sites and believed to be one of the oldest settlements in the central Nile valley, dating to around 7000 BC.

uruk-period.name: Uruk period
uruk-period.summary: The era, roughly 4000 to 3100 BC, when the first cities and states arose in Mesopotamia, named after the city of Uruk where innovations like the potter's wheel appeared.

menes.name: Menes
menes.summary: A pharaoh credited by tradition with uniting Upper and Lower Egypt and founding its First Dynasty around 3100 BC, often identified with the ruler Narmer.

naqada-iii.name: Naqada III
naqada-iii.summary: The final Predynastic phase of Egypt, roughly 3325–3000 BC, also called the Protodynastic Period, when named kings and state formation became visible ahead of Egypt's first dynasty.

narmer.name: Narmer
narmer.summary: An early Egyptian king around 3100 BC widely considered the unifier of Egypt and founder of its First Dynasty, often identified with the legendary king Menes.

tell-es-sakan.name: Tell es-Sakan
tell-es-sakan.summary: A Bronze Age mound near Gaza founded around 3300 BCE as a fortified Egyptian administrative colony, later a Canaanite city until about 2250 BCE.

palermo-stone.name: Palermo Stone
palermo-stone.summary: One of seven surviving fragments of an ancient Egyptian stele listing kings from the First Dynasty through the early Fifth Dynasty, probably made in the Fifth Dynasty and among Egypt's oldest surviving records.

narmer-palette.name: Narmer Palette
narmer-palette.summary: A ceremonial stone tablet from about the 31st century BC, among the earliest Egyptian records, thought to depict King Narmer's unification of Upper and Lower Egypt.

narmer-macehead.name: Narmer Macehead
narmer-macehead.summary: An ancient decorated stone mace head found in 1898 at Hierakonpolis, dated to King Narmer's reign around the 31st century BC and now held at Oxford's Ashmolean Museum.

manetho.name: Manetho
manetho.summary: An Egyptian priest under the Ptolemaic Kingdom (fl. 290–260 BCE) who wrote the Aegyptiaca, a Greek history of Egypt organizing its rulers into the dynasties still used today.

aegyptiaca.name: Aegyptiaca
aegyptiaca.summary: Greek-language history of ancient Egypt written by the priest Manetho around 290–260 BCE, organizing Egyptian rulers into thirty-one dynasties.

christopher-ehret.name: Christopher Ehret
christopher-ehret.summary: American scholar of African history and historical linguistics (1941–2025), a UCLA professor for nearly fifty years known for linking language reconstruction with the archaeological record.

abydos-egypt.name: Abydos
abydos-egypt.summary: One of ancient Egypt's oldest cities, home to a royal necropolis of early pharaohs and the memorial temple of Seti I.

hor-aha.name: Hor-Aha
hor-aha.summary: Considered by most Egyptologists the second pharaoh of Egypt's First Dynasty (others say the first), reigning around the 31st century BC for a long period.

nekhbet.name: Nekhbet
nekhbet.summary: An early Egyptian goddess who became patron of Upper Egypt and, alongside Wadjet, one of the two patron deities of unified ancient Egypt.

wadjet.name: Wadjet
wadjet.summary: Ancient Egyptian goddess of the city of Dep or Buto in Lower Egypt, worshipped from the Predynastic period onward and closely linked to the protective Eye of Ra and Eye of Horus.

nebty-name.name: Nebty name
nebty-name.summary: One of the 'great five names' used by Egyptian pharaohs and among the oldest royal titles, linking the king with the goddesses Nekhbet and Wadjet.

horus-name.name: Horus Name
horus-name.summary: The oldest known royal title of ancient Egyptian rulers, one of the pharaoh's 'great five names,' marked by a falcon symbol atop a serekh, and later also used by some queens.

scorpion-ii.name: Scorpion II
scorpion-ii.summary: A ruler during Egypt's Protodynastic Period of Upper Egypt, reigning around 3200 to 3000 BC, also known as King Scorpion.

cylinder-seal.name: Cylinder seal
cylinder-seal.summary: Small engraved cylinder rolled onto wet clay to leave an impression, invented around 3500 BC in the Near East and linked to the development of cuneiform writing.

sed-festival.name: Sed festival
sed-festival.summary: An ancient Egyptian ceremony celebrating a pharaoh's continued rule, typically held after thirty years on the throne and then every three to four years, involving processions and religious rites.

naqada.name: Naqada
naqada.summary: A town on the Nile's west bank in Egypt, site of an ancient cemetery of about 2,000 graves first excavated by Flinders Petrie in 1894.

qift.name: Qift (Koptos)
qift.summary: Ancient Egyptian city on the Nile near Luxor, known in Greek as Koptos, that served as a key trading link to the Red Sea and a starting point for expeditions to Punt.
